transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi. Um, well, what brings me in is that I’ve just been waking up with this... this heavy, hollow sadness lately. It’s kind of like—well, I'm a choreographer, and it feels like the studio lights are on, but there’s just no music in me anymore. I just feel really down.
Have you ever had a distinct period when you felt unusually euphoric or intensely energized compared with your usual self?

Yeah, I have. Um, there were stretches where I felt just... dazzlingly alive, I guess you could say. Like I had all this intense energy. But then, I would get suddenly furious if anyone questioned the plan, or... or if they reminded me that my ankle still needed rest. It was just this huge rush of energy, but it could turn into anger really fast if someone tried to slow me down.
During those unusually energized stretches, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Yeah, my sleep has been kind of all over the place. Back then, during those energized stretches... I didn't really need much rest at all. Some nights I just stayed up sketching formations until dawn and felt fine. But lately, it's different. I'll fall asleep completely exhausted, but then I wake up at four or five in the morning, and my stomach is just tight.
How long did those unusually energized periods typically last?
I'm not really sure, honestly. I didn't exactly keep track of the days when it was happening. It felt like a while, but I couldn't give you a specific number of days or weeks.
What is the longest stretch you can remember when you felt unusually energized and needed very little sleep?

Honestly, I really don't know. Like I said, I wasn't keeping a calendar or anything. It just... it felt like it went on for a while, maybe a few weeks? But I couldn't tell you the exact longest stretch. I just remember it happening.
During those unusually energized periods, did they cause major problems in your work or relationships?

Yeah, they did cause some issues with my work. Um, I fell behind on my teaching prep, and I actually missed a grant deadline. The studio just got so chaotic that my collaborators had to start handling basic scheduling for me. 

I mean, I'm still showing up for the essentials, but... I'm just not functioning like I normally do as a choreographer or a teacher.
Can you recall whether any of those unusually energized periods lasted at least a full week?

I really can't say for sure if it was a full week straight. It might have been, but like I mentioned, the days kind of blurred together. I just know it lasted long enough to mess up my schedule and my work.
How long has this current period of sadness been going on?
The sadness? Um... I'd say the depressed part has been present for about nine months now.
During one of those energized periods, did you ever become so unusually activated or out of control that you needed emergency care or hospitalization?

No, I've never needed to go to the hospital or anything like that. I mean, things definitely got out of hand with my work and my schedule, but it never got to the point where I needed emergency care. I was still, you know, physically safe, just... really disorganized.
Was there ever a stretch of at least four days in a row when you felt unusually energized and needed very little sleep?

Um... I'm really not sure about it being exactly four days. Like I was saying before, time just sort of blurred together when I was feeling that way. I know I definitely wasn't sleeping much during those times, but I couldn't tell you for a fact if it was four days in a row.
During these nine months, have you lost interest in or stopped enjoying activities that you normally find pleasurable?
Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I still enjoy dancing and working on my choreography. Even though I've been feeling sad, I haven't really lost interest in the things I usually like to do.
During those energized periods, did your thoughts race unusually fast?.

No, I don't think so. I mean, I had a lot of ideas for my choreography and things I wanted to do, but my mind didn't really feel like it was going unusually fast or anything. My thoughts felt pretty normal to me, I just... I just had a lot of physical energy.
During those energized periods, did you feel unusually powerful, talented, or important compared with your usual self?

Yeah, I think I did. Um, I remember I had this setback, and I honestly believed I could turn it into this huge, career-defining work. Like, I thought it was going to completely change how people think about dance and the wilderness. I felt so sure of my talent and what I was doing, and... well, I was actually really shocked when other people didn't immediately see my vision for it.
During those energized periods, did other people comment that you were talking much more or faster than usual?

Yes, they did. Um, my collaborators actually told me I was talking so fast in our meetings that they couldn’t even get a word in. I didn't really realize I was doing it, but I just remember feeling like... if I paused, even for a second, the whole idea would just disappear. So I felt like I had to get it all out right then.
Can you remember one specific energized period when your unusually high energy or irritability lasted continuously for at least four days before your mood returned to its usual level?

Um, I'm not really sure. I mean, I know I had that high energy, but I didn't really track the days. I can't remember a specific time where I could say for sure that it lasted four days continuously before I went back to normal. The timeline is just... a bit blurry for me, so I don't really know exactly how long those periods lasted.
During this nine-month period of sadness, have you had noticeably less energy than usual?

Yes, definitely. I just feel... completely wiped out after really small things. Like, even just answering one single email to a dancer, or trying to take a shower with this ankle brace on. It takes everything out of me. And the frustrating part is that lying down doesn’t really recharge me either. I just stay tired.
Was there any specific stretch when you felt unusually energized and needed very little sleep for four days in a row?

I'm really not sure about the exact number of days. Like I said before, the timeline is just kind of a blur to me. I know I had periods where I didn't need much sleep and felt really energized, but I couldn't tell you if it was exactly four days in a row. I just didn't keep track of it like that.
During one of those energized stretches, was the unusually elevated or irritable mood present most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes, during those times, it was pretty much all day. Like, I would wake up feeling just... dazzlingly alive, you know? Like I could do anything. But then, almost out of nowhere, I'd get furious. Especially if someone questioned my plans or... or reminded me that my ankle still needed to rest. It was just this constant back and forth between feeling amazing and being really angry, pretty much the whole day.
Can you identify any one period when your unusually energized or irritable mood lasted continuously for at least four days in a row?

I really can't say for sure. Like I mentioned, I didn't keep track of the days. I know those energized periods lasted for a while, but I couldn't swear to it being exactly four days continuously. It just all blends together when I try to look back at it.
What is the longest uninterrupted period when you felt unusually energized or irritable, with much less need for sleep?

I really don't know the exact longest stretch. It's just hard to put a number on it. I know it went on for a bit, but as far as the maximum number of days without a break... I just didn't measure it like that. It felt like a long time while I was in it, but I can't give you a specific length.
